subject: Transient read-only activation & runtime kernel pin instructions
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: ops@atlasware.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transient read-only activation & runtime kernel pin instructions

Hi team —

Quick heads-up: we’ve observed a recurring memory-corruption signature on a small subset of Atlasware inference requests (A100s, driver 520.x) when input sequence lengths spike above ~12k tokens. Impact has been contained but we see a growing rate of request-level failures and an uptick in aborted sessions in the last 45m.

Immediate mitigations we recommend (short notice, <60m window):
- Enable transient read-only mode for Atlasware routing (this prevents write-path hot paths on the KV cache while keeping read latency within SLO).
- Apply kernel pin to the 510.85 CUDA kernel on the affected pools to avoid the regression introduced in 520.

Why this path: it keeps serving mostly online, prevents state-corrupting write races during the window, and avoids a full region failover. The kernel pin is reversible without model restarts; read-only mode requires route config flip but is low-risk.

Action items for Atlasware ops:
1) Confirm you accept transient read-only for your PROD routing for the next 90 minutes. This will make writes (cache fills, kv-evict ops) deferred and may increase downstream token-caching misses by ~3-8%.
2) Provide a single point contact (email or Slack) so we can coordinate the switchback.

Internal notes: Marissa, Karthik — I need the kernel pin command and a short rollback script in the thread. Evelyn — please add incident log (attached) to the incident record and open a JIRA if not already.

Attachments: runtime-incident-sample.log (snippets), kernel-pin-instructions.md

I’ll wait for Atlasware ops confirmation before executing.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: j.kim@atlasware.com <j.kim@atlasware.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:29:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transient read-only activation & runtime kernel pin instructions

Sean —

Thanks for the quick detection and suggested mitigations. We accept the transient read-only activation for the next 90 minutes. Our on-call is ready to monitor and we’ll provide a Slack bridge (ops-atlasware) in two minutes.

Can you confirm whether the kernel pin will affect other shared tenants in the same cell? We run a small burst pool shared with a partner but we can isolate if required.

—Jae (Atlasware ops)
ops@atlasware.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, ops@atlasware.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:35:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transient read-only activation & runtime kernel pin instructions

Sean / team —

Confirmed plan and commands below. I ran the kernel pin in staging (same driver family) and validated smoke traffic for 15m. Expected impact: no model restarts, small CPU scheduler jitter for pinned kernels during active roll. We’ll perform a pinned-driver rollout on the specified pool id: pool-us-west-3-a100-33.

Kernel pin steps (high-level):
1) curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.ai/pools/pool-us-west-3-a100-33/actions/pin-kernel -d '{"kernel":"cuda-510.85"}' 
2) Watch /ops/pools/pool-us-west-3-a100-33/health for CUDA kernel state; target transition <= 5m
3) If >10% latency spike or >2% error increase, run rollback: curl -X POST .../actions/unpin-kernel

Read-only route flip (to be executed only after Atlasware confirms):
- POST to /routing/atlasware/prod with body {"prefix_mode":"ro-transient","duration_minutes":90} 

Rollback plan: after 90 minutes, we unflip routing and unpin kernel (order: unpin then unflip). Rationale: unpin first so any cached kernel calls revert to default then allow write-paths again.

I’ve attached a short script (kernel-pin-instructions.md) and included the minimal rollback commands. I will be on the bridge.

—Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: ops@atlasware.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transient read-only activation & runtime kernel pin instructions

Update + close loop:

Timeline: 09:42 — Atlasware confirmed. 09:48 — Read-only routing flip executed. 09:50 — Kernel pin applied to pool-us-west-3-a100-33. 09:58 — Observed immediate drop in aborted sessions; error rate for the impacted signature down from 2.1% -> 0.06% on inspected traffic.

Status now: serving stabilised for Atlasware PROD. We will keep the transient read-only mode active for the requested 90 minutes and then unpin the kernel at +60m for validation, followed by unflip at +90m.

Next steps / follow-up:
- Postmortem: I’m scheduling a short postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 PDT to cover root cause analysis and long-term remediation (probable driver backport or targeted kernel guard). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270502-07
- Atlasware, please review the attached runtime log sample and confirm SLA telemetry we should include in the postmortem.

Attachments: runtime-incident-sample.log, kernel-pin-instructions.md

Thanks everyone for the fast coordination. I’ll send the postmortem invite shortly.

—Sean
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
